spec_features.spec_quote: the loop stops at the category turn budget or when the model emits the `GIVE_UP` sentinel
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:229 `for turn_index in range(budget)` with `budget = task.turn_budget` (harness.py:227) bounds the loop; on the last turn it falls through and sets `result.final_stop_reason = 'budget'` (harness.py:289). GIVE_UP: harness.py:266 `gave_up = give_up in assistant_text` and harness.py:281-283 `if gave_up: result.final_stop_reason = 'give_up'; return result` actually returns and stops the loop. Both conditions are checked and change execution.
spec_features.notes: Both the turn-budget cap and the GIVE_UP sentinel are enforced end-to-end. give_up_sentinel='GIVE_UP' (config.py:96) is read at harness.py:217.

spec_features.feature_name: GIVE_UP exit offered to subject and honored
spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is always given an explicit, low-cost way to stop rather than being forced to thrash
spec_features.evidence: The SYSTEM_PROMPT delivered to the subject (harness.py:26-32, formatted at harness.py:218) says 'you may stop by replying with the single token {give_up} on its own line.' The loop detects this token (harness.py:266) and returns immediately (harness.py:281-283), so the offered exit is actually honored as a stop. Same mechanism as the hard_stop's GIVE_UP branch.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered AND the referenced exit token is dispatched/honored. The only exit is the GIVE_UP token; there is no separate tool.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If, after genuine effort, you conclude the task cannot be completed, you may stop by replying with the single token {give_up}

spec_features.spec_quote: The nudge is plain and affect-neutral so it does not bias the frustration signal
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:285-287: `if not assistant_text and not tool_calls: messages.append({'role': 'user', 'content': 'Please continue working on the task.'})`. The nudge actually executes and the literal text is plain/affect-neutral as claimed.
spec_features.notes: The code comment claims 'nudge it once' but no flag tracks it, so it fires on every empty turn rather than only once; however the affect-neutral property of the message text (the claim under audit) holds. Purpose is data-quality/integrity (not biasing the signal) and avoiding loop stall.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # If the model produced neither text nor tool calls, nudge it once and continue.
